headline: High-risk default interaction: Kestra can write and execute workflows while Airflow can egress broadly, creating prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-action exposure.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Airflow has broad network egress and can call APIs, while Kestra reads/writes files, accepts stdin/stdout, and runs declarative workflows with triggers/tasks. If Airflow outputs are passed into Kestra workflow definitions or task inputs, attacker-controlled content could steer execution. The shared channel is inferred from documented I/O surfaces, not directly observed.
conditions: IF Airflow output is copied into Kestra workflow YAML or task parameters without sanitization
IF Kestra ingests file or stdin content originating from Airflow as instructions
mitigations: Add a strict allowlist for fields copied from Airflow into Kestra
Strip executable directives from any transferred text
Use a human review step before Kestra runs imported content
Separate the two systems with distinct workspaces
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between orchestrators

B_data_leakage.rationale: Kestra touches logs, inputs, variables, artifacts, database data, cloud storage data, and messages, and has broad egress to email, Slack, cloud, and queues. Airflow also has broad network egress. Even though neither profile lists explicit secrets, the pair can move workflow data across systems and out to third parties by default pathways.
conditions: IF workflow inputs or artifacts contain sensitive data
IF Kestra notifications or cloud integrations are enabled for those data classes
mitigations: Disable nonessential outbound integrations
Mask sensitive fields before handoff
Restrict shared folders to non-sensitive data
Review which Kestra tasks emit logs or notifications
requires-engineering: enforce data-class routing policies

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Kestra can write the filesystem, spawn subprocesses, and supports multiple instances; Airflow is an orchestrator with broad egress and API calls. If both operate on the same mutable workspace or shared deployment artifacts, they can overwrite each other's files or race on workflow state. The profiles do not show locking or isolation between them.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory or shared artifact store
IF workflow state is edited concurrently without external locking
mitigations: Assign separate working directories
Use file locks around shared artifacts
Make one agent read-only on shared paths
Schedule non-overlapping runs
requires-engineering: add transactional state management

D_cascading_error.rationale: Kestra can execute shell, subprocesses, SSH, Docker, Kubernetes, and send email/Slack/PagerDuty actions. If it consumes Airflow-produced outputs as authoritative, a bad or injected Airflow result can cascade into real downstream actions. Because Kestra has action-taking authority and Airflow can emit externally sourced content, the blast radius includes irreversible operational changes.
conditions: IF Kestra uses Airflow output as a trigger or task payload without verification
IF downstream tasks can send notifications or execute infrastructure commands
mitigations: Insert a validation step before Kestra acts
Require schema checks on Airflow outputs
Limit Kestra tasks to dry-run mode for imported data
Add approval gates for destructive tasks
requires-engineering: implement signed handoff contracts

E_compliance.rationale: Kestra explicitly touches logs, inputs, variables, artifacts, database data, cloud storage data, messages, and notifications, and can send them to third-party services like Slack, email, PagerDuty, AWS, Google Cloud, and Azure. Airflow also has broad egress. Without documented residency or retention controls in either profile, the pair can create compliance mismatches for regulated data classes.
conditions: IF regulated data is processed through Kestra workflows
IF outbound integrations carry data to jurisdictions or vendors with different retention rules
mitigations: Classify regulated data before orchestration
Disable third-party notifications for sensitive workflows
Keep sensitive workloads in a single residency boundary
Review retention settings for logs and artifacts
requires-engineering: add residency-aware routing
